title: Input-gradient space particle inference for neural network ensembles

en.text: A deep ensemble is a blunt instrument that works surprisingly well: train the same network a handful of times from different random seeds, average their predictions, and you usually get better accuracy, better calibration, and more graceful behavior on inputs the model has never seen. The reason is diversity. Each member settles into a different explanation of the data, and their disagreement is exactly what makes the average trustworthy.

So a natural idea is to stop leaving that diversity to chance and start enforcing it. Particle-based variational inference does this by treating each network as a particle and adding a repulsion term that actively pushes members apart during training. The catch is a question that turns out to matter a great deal: in what space should the members be pushed apart? Repel them in weight space and you fight against the fact that neural networks are wildly over-parameterized, so countless different weight vectors encode the same function. Repel them in function space and you run into an intractable comparison between whole functions, which forces shortcuts that tend to make the models underfit. In practice, neither approach had improved much on a plain deep ensemble.

This paper, First-order Repulsive Deep Ensembles (FoRDE), proposes a third space to disagree in. Instead of comparing weights or outputs, it pushes members apart in the space of their input gradients, the derivatives of the output with respect to the input. The choice is not cosmetic: input gradients characterize a function up to a translation, they are the same small size as the input rather than the enormous weight vector, and forcing them to differ forces each network to lean on different input features. The result is an ensemble that is markedly more robust and better calibrated when the input is corrupted.

en.caption: Figure 1. Input-gradient repulsion in a 1D regression toy problem with three networks. Left: early in training the three models fit the data but agree almost everywhere, so functional diversity is low. Middle: the repulsion term pushes the members' input gradients (the arrows) apart on a unit circle at each data point. Right: by the end of training the three functions have genuinely diverged, gaining the diversity that makes an ensemble useful.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02775 · Code: https://github.com/AaltoPML/FoRDE
Why the space of repulsion matters

To see why input gradients are a good place to enforce disagreement, it helps to compare the three views of a neural network. Its weights are what you optimize, but they are a poor handle on diversity: over-parameterization means two very different weight vectors can compute the exact same function, so pushing weights apart can waste effort without changing behavior at all. Its function values are what you ultimately care about, but comparing entire functions requires a kernel over function space that is expensive to evaluate; earlier repulsive methods approximated it on training inputs only, which nudged the models toward underfitting and left little real gain over a vanilla ensemble.

Input gradients sit between these two extremes. A function is determined, up to an additive constant, by its gradient field, so two networks with different input gradients are guaranteed to be different functions, not redundant re-parameterizations. And a gradient has the dimensionality of the input, which for an image is far smaller than the weight vector, so it is cheap to compare with a kernel. There is a bonus that turns out to be the crux of the empirical story: the input gradient tells you which input features a network is sensitive to. Make two members' gradients point in different directions and you have made them attend to complementary features, which is precisely the property you want when the input is later perturbed.
How FoRDE trains

FoRDE is built on Wasserstein gradient descent, a particle-based flavor of variational inference. Every ensemble member is a particle, and each update combines two forces. A driving force pulls the particle toward high-density regions of the Bayesian posterior, which is essentially ordinary training with a prior. A repulsion force, weighted by a kernel, pushes the particle away from the others. Everything hinges on what that kernel compares.

FoRDE's kernel compares the input gradient of the true-label logit, averaged over the training data, after normalizing each gradient to unit length. Two design decisions make this practical. First, using only the true-label gradient rather than the full Jacobian keeps the cost linear in the number of training samples. Second, normalizing to the unit sphere and comparing directions matters because gradient magnitudes shrink as training converges; comparing directions keeps the repulsion meaningful late in training and is what encourages members to rely on complementary features. On top of an RBF base kernel, FoRDE sets the per-dimension lengthscales from a Principal Component Analysis of the data, so repulsion is strongest along the most informative input directions. The authors show this data-driven kernel behaves much like a feature-robustness prior (EmpCov), which is a clean explanation for why the robustness gains appear.
Evidence that the diversity is real

Before the large-scale numbers, two toy problems make the mechanism visible. In 1D regression, the honest test of an ensemble is what it does away from the training data: a diverse ensemble should spread out and report high uncertainty where it has seen nothing. FoRDE fans out noticeably more than a deep ensemble or the weight- and function-space repulsive variants.

en.caption: Figure 2. Predictive uncertainty in 1D regression. Away from the data clusters, FoRDE (right) spreads into a visibly wider band than the deep ensemble, Weight-RDE, and Function-RDE baselines, indicating greater functional diversity where it matters most.

en.text: The 2D classification task tells the same story in the plane. Measuring the entropy of the predictive posterior, FoRDE is the only method that stays uncertain across essentially all regions outside the training clusters, rather than confidently extrapolating a sharp decision boundary into territory where it has no real basis for that confidence.

en.caption: Figure 3. Predictive-entropy maps for a 2D classification problem. Warmer regions are confident, cooler regions uncertain. FoRDE (right) keeps high uncertainty across the whole input plane outside the labeled clusters, while the baselines commit confidently far from any data.

en.text: Robustness under corruption

The main experiments run on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet with ResNet-18 and PreActResNet-18 backbones and ten-member ensembles. Robustness is measured on the corrupted benchmarks CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, and TinyImageNet-C, which apply 19 corruption types at 5 severity levels, reporting corruption accuracy (cA), corruption NLL, and corruption ECE alongside their clean counterparts. The pattern is consistent: FoRDE with PCA lengthscales is the strongest method on every corruption metric while staying competitive on clean data. Against the second-best method it improves accuracy by about +2.4% on CIFAR-10-C and +1.3% on CIFAR-100-C.

en.caption: Table 1. Clean accuracy and corruption accuracy (cA) on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18, 10-member ensembles, averaged over 5 seeds. FoRDE-PCA stays within a fraction of a point of the best clean accuracy while clearly leading under corruption.
en.note: Higher is better for all columns. C10-C / C100-C are the corrupted benchmarks (19 corruption types x 5 severities). Numbers from Tables 1 and 2 of the paper.

en.text: The transfer-learning experiments broaden the picture across NLL, ECE, accuracy, and epistemic uncertainty, under both natural distribution shift (CINIC-10) and corruption shift. FoRDE improves on the baselines across the board, and its higher epistemic uncertainty on out-of-distribution data is a direct readout of the extra functional diversity that the method is explicitly designed to produce.

en.caption: Figure 4. Transfer-learning results. Across NLL, ECE, and accuracy on in-distribution, naturally shifted (CINIC-10), and corrupted test sets, FoRDE matches or beats the baselines; the rightmost panels show it also carries the highest epistemic uncertainty on out-of-distribution data, the signature of greater functional diversity.

en.text: Where the lengthscales come from, and what they cost

The kernel lengthscales are the knob that decides how repulsion is spread across input dimensions, and the paper ablates them carefully. PCA lengthscales, which emphasize high-variance features, give the best corruption robustness. Identity lengthscales instead give the best clean accuracy on CIFAR-100 and the best NLL on CIFAR-10, at the price of slightly weaker robustness. A tuned interpolation between the two extremes, FoRDE-Tuned, tends to win on both clean and corrupted data. A separate study on WideResNet-16x4 makes the efficiency of the diversity concrete: a 10-member FoRDE matches or beats the corruption robustness of a 30-member deep ensemble, though it trails a deep ensemble slightly on clean data.

None of this is free. Each update needs an extra forward-backward pass to compute input gradients, so FoRDE trains about three times as long as a plain deep ensemble (roughly 101 seconds per epoch on an A100). The trade is worth it when the deployment cares about corrupted or shifted inputs, which is exactly where FoRDE pulls ahead.
Takeaway

The lasting lesson is that the space in which you enforce diversity matters as much as how hard you enforce it. Weight space is wasteful because of over-parameterization; function space is intractable to compare directly. Input gradients sit in between: small enough to compare cheaply, expressive enough to make members genuinely different functions, and meaningful enough that pushing them apart makes members rely on complementary features. Paired with data-driven PCA lengthscales, that choice buys more robust, better-calibrated ensembles under real-world input corruptions, at about three times the training cost.

zh.text: 深度集成（Deep Ensemble）是一种「简单却出奇有效」的做法：用不同随机种子把同一个网络训练好几遍，再把它们的预测取平均，往往就能同时拿到更高的准确率、更好的校准（calibration），以及在没见过的输入上更稳的表现。它之所以有效，关键在于多样性（diversity）：每个成员都落到了对数据的一种不同解释上，而它们之间的分歧，正是「取平均」值得信任的原因。

于是一个自然的想法是：不要把多样性交给运气，而是主动去制造它。基于粒子的变分推断（particle-based variational inference）就是这么做的：把每个网络当作一个粒子，在训练中加入一项互斥力（repulsion），主动把成员往两边推开。但这里藏着一个影响很大的问题：应该在哪个空间里把成员推开？在权重空间（weight space）里推，会和「神经网络严重过参数化」这个事实作对，因为无数个不同的权重其实编码的是同一个函数；在函数空间（function space）里推，又要面对「比较两个完整函数」这种难以计算的操作，逼着方法走近似捷径，反而容易欠拟合。结果是：这两条路都没能比普通深度集成好多少。

本文提出的 FoRDE（First-order Repulsive Deep Ensembles，一阶互斥深度集成）给出了第三个「制造分歧」的空间。它不比较权重，也不比较输出，而是在输入梯度（input gradient，即输出对输入的导数）空间里把成员推开。这个选择并不只是换个说法：输入梯度可以在「相差一个平移」的意义上唯一刻画一个函数；它的维度和输入一样小，远小于庞大的权重向量；而且强迫成员的输入梯度不同，等于强迫每个网络去依赖不同的输入特征。最终得到的集成，在输入被损坏（corruption）时明显更鲁棒、校准也更好。

zh.caption: 图1 一维回归玩具问题中，三个网络的输入梯度互斥过程。左：训练早期，三个模型都拟合了数据，却几乎处处一致，功能多样性很低。中：互斥项在每个数据点上，把成员的输入梯度（箭头）沿单位圆推开。右：训练结束时，三条函数真正分开，获得了让集成有价值的多样性。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02775 · 代码：https://github.com/AaltoPML/FoRDE
为什么「在哪个空间互斥」如此关键

要理解为什么输入梯度是个好地方，可以把神经网络的三种「视角」摆在一起比。权重是我们真正在优化的东西，但它并不适合用来衡量多样性：过参数化意味着两个差别很大的权重向量可能算出完全相同的函数，所以在权重空间里互相推开，可能白费力气，行为却没变。函数值是我们最终真正关心的，但比较完整的函数需要一个定义在函数空间上的核，计算代价很高；早期的互斥方法只能在训练输入上近似它，结果把模型推向欠拟合，相比普通集成几乎没有真实收益。

输入梯度恰好落在这两个极端之间。一个函数在「相差一个常数」的意义上由它的梯度场决定，所以两个网络只要输入梯度不同，就一定是不同的函数，而不是同一个函数的冗余改写。同时，梯度的维度和输入一样，对图像来说远小于权重向量，用核比较起来很便宜。还有一个后来被证明是实证关键的额外好处：输入梯度告诉你一个网络对哪些输入特征敏感。让两个成员的梯度指向不同方向，就等于让它们关注互补的特征，而这恰恰是输入之后被扰动时你最希望模型具备的性质。
FoRDE 是怎么训练的
FoRDE 建立在 Wasserstein 梯度下降之上，这是一种基于粒子的变分推断。集成里的每个成员都是一个粒子，每次更新都由两股力组成：驱动力（driving force）把粒子拉向贝叶斯后验的高密度区域，本质上就是带先验的普通训练；互斥力（repulsion force）则由一个核加权，把粒子从其他成员那里推开。一切的关键，都落在这个核到底比较什么。

FoRDE 的核比较的是「真实标签对应 logit」的输入梯度，在训练数据上取平均，并且先把每个梯度归一化到单位长度。两个设计让它变得可行：其一，只用真实标签的梯度、而不是完整的雅可比矩阵，让计算代价对训练样本数保持线性；其二，归一化到单位球、比较方向很重要，因为随着训练收敛，梯度的模会不断变小，比较方向能让互斥在训练后期依然有意义，也正是它促使成员去依赖互补特征。在 RBF 基核之上，FoRDE 用数据的主成分分析（PCA）来设定每个维度的长度尺度（lengthscale），使互斥在信息量最大的输入方向上最强。作者指出，这个数据驱动的核，行为上很接近一种特征鲁棒性先验（EmpCov），这也干净地解释了鲁棒性收益的来源。
多样性是真的吗：两个玩具实验
在大规模数字之前，两个玩具问题先把机制变得可见。在一维回归里，检验集成是否诚实的方式，是看它在远离训练数据的地方怎么表现：一个多样的集成应当在没见过的区域散开、报告高不确定性。FoRDE 明显比深度集成、以及权重空间和函数空间的互斥变体散得更开。

zh.caption: 图2 一维回归中的预测不确定性。在远离数据簇的区域，FoRDE（最右）散成明显更宽的置信带，超过深度集成、Weight-RDE 和 Function-RDE，说明它在最需要的地方拥有更强的功能多样性。

zh.text: 二维分类任务在平面上讲了同一个故事。用预测后验的熵来衡量，FoRDE 是唯一一个在训练簇之外几乎所有区域都保持不确定的方法，而不会在它本没有理由自信的地方，把一条清晰的决策边界自信地外推出去。

zh.caption: 图3 二维分类问题的预测熵图。暖色代表自信、冷色代表不确定。FoRDE（最右）在标注簇之外的整个输入平面上都保持高不确定性，而各基线在远离数据处仍然自信地下结论。

zh.text: 损坏输入下的鲁棒性

主实验在 CIFAR-10、CIFAR-100 和 TinyImageNet 上进行，骨干网络为 ResNet-18 与 PreActResNet-18，集成含 10 个成员。鲁棒性在损坏基准 CIFAR-10-C、CIFAR-100-C 和 TinyImageNet-C 上测量，这些基准施加 19 种损坏类型、每种 5 个严重等级，并在干净指标之外报告损坏准确率（cA）、损坏 NLL 和损坏 ECE。结论一致：采用 PCA 长度尺度的 FoRDE 在每一项损坏指标上都是最强的，同时在干净数据上保持有竞争力。相比第二名，它在 CIFAR-10-C 上准确率提升约 +2.4%，在 CIFAR-100-C 上提升约 +1.3%。

zh.caption: 表1 ResNet-18、10 成员集成在 CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 上的干净准确率与损坏准确率（cA），5 个随机种子平均。FoRDE-PCA 干净准确率与最优仅差零点几个百分点，损坏下则明显领先。
zh.note: 所有列均为越高越好。C10-C / C100-C 为损坏基准（19 种损坏类型 × 5 个严重等级）。数字取自论文表 1 与表 2。

zh.text: 迁移学习实验把画面进一步铺开，覆盖 NLL、ECE、准确率和认知不确定性（epistemic uncertainty），并同时考察自然分布偏移（CINIC-10）和损坏偏移。FoRDE 在各项上都优于基线，而它在分布外数据上更高的认知不确定性，正是这套方法所要制造的额外功能多样性的直接读数。

zh.caption: 图4 迁移学习结果。在同分布、自然偏移（CINIC-10）与损坏测试集上，FoRDE 在 NLL、ECE 和准确率上都追平或超过基线；最右两列显示它在分布外数据上还拥有最高的认知不确定性，这正是更强功能多样性的标志。

zh.text: 长度尺度从哪来，代价是什么

核的长度尺度决定了互斥如何分布到各个输入维度上，是本文重点消融的旋钮。强调高方差特征的 PCA 长度尺度带来最好的损坏鲁棒性；恒等（Identity）长度尺度则在 CIFAR-100 上给出最好的干净准确率、在 CIFAR-10 上给出最好的 NLL，代价是鲁棒性略弱；在两个极端之间做加权插值的 FoRDE-Tuned，往往能在干净和损坏数据上都取胜。另一项在 WideResNet-16x4 上的研究，把这种多样性的「性价比」讲得很具体：一个 10 成员的 FoRDE，在损坏鲁棒性上追平甚至超过一个 30 成员的深度集成，尽管在干净数据上略逊于深度集成。
这一切并非免费。由于每次更新都要额外做一次前向-反向传播来计算输入梯度，FoRDE 的训练时间大约是普通深度集成的三倍（在作者的 A100 设置下约为每轮 101 秒）。这笔账是否划算，取决于部署场景有多在意损坏或偏移的输入，而那恰恰是 FoRDE 拉开差距的区间。
小结

FoRDE 留下的长久启示是：你在哪个空间里强制多样性，和你强制多大力度同样重要。权重空间因为过参数化而浪费；函数空间难以直接比较；输入梯度恰好是两者之间的甜蜜点——足够小，比较起来便宜；足够有表达力，能保证成员成为不同的函数；又足够有语义，把它们推开就等于让成员依赖互补特征。再配上数据驱动的 PCA 长度尺度，这个选择换来的，是在真实世界常见的那类输入损坏下更鲁棒、更好校准的集成，代价大约是三倍的训练时间。

en.title: From weights to input gradients: a cheaper place to make ensembles disagree
en.subtitle: FoRDE (ICLR 2024) repels ensemble members in input-gradient space, and the payoff shows up under image corruptions.

en.title: From weights to input gradients: a cheaper place to make ensembles disagree
en.subtitle: FoRDE (ICLR 2024) repels ensemble members in input-gradient space, and the payoff shows up under image corruptions.

zh.title: 让集成模型「学会不一样」，换个空间成本更低
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · FoRDE：在输入梯度空间中互斥集成成员，换来图像损坏下更强的鲁棒性与校准。

en.caption: Figure 1. Input-gradient repulsion in a 1D regression toy problem with three networks. Left: early in training the three models fit the data but agree almost everywhere, so functional diversity is low. Middle: the repulsion term pushes the members' input gradients (the arrows) apart on a unit circle at each data point. Right: by the end of training the three functions have genuinely diverged, gaining the diversity that makes an ensemble useful.

en.text: Why the space of repulsion matters

To see why input gradients are a good place to enforce disagreement, it helps to compare the three views of a neural network. Its weights are what you optimize, but they are a poor handle on diversity: over-parameterization means two very different weight vectors can compute the exact same function, so pushing weights apart can waste effort without changing behavior at all. Its function values are what you ultimately care about, but comparing entire functions requires a kernel over function space that is expensive to evaluate; earlier repulsive methods approximated it on training inputs only, which nudged the models toward underfitting and left little real gain over a vanilla ensemble.

Input gradients sit between these two extremes. A function is determined, up to an additive constant, by its gradient field, so two networks with different input gradients are guaranteed to be different functions, not redundant re-parameterizations. And a gradient has the dimensionality of the input, which for an image is far smaller than the weight vector, so it is cheap to compare with a kernel. There is a bonus that turns out to be the crux of the empirical story: the input gradient tells you which input features a network is sensitive to. Make two members' gradients point in different directions and you have made them attend to complementary features, which is precisely the property you want when the input is later perturbed.

zh.caption: 图1 一维回归玩具问题中，三个网络的输入梯度互斥过程。左：训练早期，三个模型都拟合了数据，却几乎处处一致，功能多样性很低。中：互斥项在每个数据点上，把成员的输入梯度（箭头）沿单位圆推开。右：训练结束时，三条函数真正分开，获得了让集成有价值的多样性。

zh.text: 为什么「在哪个空间互斥」如此关键

要理解为什么输入梯度是个好地方，可以把神经网络的三种「视角」摆在一起比。权重是我们真正在优化的东西，但它并不适合用来衡量多样性：过参数化意味着两个差别很大的权重向量可能算出完全相同的函数，所以在权重空间里互相推开，可能白费力气，行为却没变。函数值是我们最终真正关心的，但比较完整的函数需要一个定义在函数空间上的核，计算代价很高；早期的互斥方法只能在训练输入上近似它，结果把模型推向欠拟合，相比普通集成几乎没有真实收益。

输入梯度恰好落在这两个极端之间。一个函数在「相差一个常数」的意义上由它的梯度场决定，所以两个网络只要输入梯度不同，就一定是不同的函数，而不是同一个函数的冗余改写。同时，梯度的维度和输入一样，对图像来说远小于权重向量，用核比较起来很便宜。还有一个后来被证明是实证关键的额外好处：输入梯度告诉你一个网络对哪些输入特征敏感。让两个成员的梯度指向不同方向，就等于让它们关注互补的特征，而这恰恰是输入之后被扰动时你最希望模型具备的性质。

zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · FoRDE：在输入梯度空间中互斥集成成员，换来图像损坏下更强的鲁棒性与校准。

en.caption: Figure 1. Input-gradient repulsion in a 1D regression toy problem with three networks. Left: early in training the three models fit the data but agree almost everywhere, so functional diversity is low. Middle: the repulsion term pushes the members' input gradients (the arrows) apart on a unit circle at each data point. Right: by the end of training the three functions have genuinely diverged, gaining the diversity that makes an ensemble useful.

en.text: How FoRDE trains

FoRDE is built on Wasserstein gradient descent, a particle-based flavor of variational inference. Every ensemble member is a particle, and each update combines two forces. A driving force pulls the particle toward high-density regions of the Bayesian posterior, which is essentially ordinary training with a prior. A repulsion force, weighted by a kernel, pushes the particle away from the others. Everything hinges on what that kernel compares.

FoRDE's kernel compares the input gradient of the true-label logit, averaged over the training data, after normalizing each gradient to unit length. Two design decisions make this practical. First, using only the true-label gradient rather than the full Jacobian keeps the cost linear in the number of training samples. Second, normalizing to the unit sphere and comparing directions matters because gradient magnitudes shrink as training converges; comparing directions keeps the repulsion meaningful late in training and is what encourages members to rely on complementary features. On top of an RBF base kernel, FoRDE sets the per-dimension lengthscales from a Principal Component Analysis of the data, so repulsion is strongest along the most informative input directions. The authors show this data-driven kernel behaves much like a feature-robustness prior (EmpCov), which is a clean explanation for why the robustness gains appear.

zh.caption: 图1 一维回归玩具问题中，三个网络的输入梯度互斥过程。左：训练早期，三个模型都拟合了数据，却几乎处处一致，功能多样性很低。中：互斥项在每个数据点上，把成员的输入梯度（箭头）沿单位圆推开。右：训练结束时，三条函数真正分开，获得了让集成有价值的多样性。

zh.text: FoRDE 是怎么训练的
FoRDE 建立在 Wasserstein 梯度下降之上，这是一种基于粒子的变分推断。集成里的每个成员都是一个粒子，每次更新都由两股力组成：驱动力（driving force）把粒子拉向贝叶斯后验的高密度区域，本质上就是带先验的普通训练；互斥力（repulsion force）则由一个核加权，把粒子从其他成员那里推开。一切的关键，都落在这个核到底比较什么。

FoRDE 的核比较的是「真实标签对应 logit」的输入梯度，在训练数据上取平均，并且先把每个梯度归一化到单位长度。两个设计让它变得可行：其一，只用真实标签的梯度、而不是完整的雅可比矩阵，让计算代价对训练样本数保持线性；其二，归一化到单位球、比较方向很重要，因为随着训练收敛，梯度的模会不断变小，比较方向能让互斥在训练后期依然有意义，也正是它促使成员去依赖互补特征。在 RBF 基核之上，FoRDE 用数据的主成分分析（PCA）来设定每个维度的长度尺度（lengthscale），使互斥在信息量最大的输入方向上最强。作者指出，这个数据驱动的核，行为上很接近一种特征鲁棒性先验（EmpCov），这也干净地解释了鲁棒性收益的来源。

en.text: Robustness under corruption

The main experiments run on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet with ResNet-18 and PreActResNet-18 backbones and ten-member ensembles. Robustness is measured on the corrupted benchmarks CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, and TinyImageNet-C, which apply 19 corruption types at 5 severity levels, reporting corruption accuracy (cA), corruption NLL, and corruption ECE alongside their clean counterparts. The pattern is consistent: FoRDE with PCA lengthscales is the strongest method on every corruption metric while staying competitive on clean data. Against the second-best method it improves accuracy by about +2.4% on CIFAR-10-C and +1.3% on CIFAR-100-C.

en.caption: Table 1. Clean accuracy and corruption accuracy (cA) on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18, 10-member ensembles, averaged over 5 seeds. FoRDE-PCA stays within a fraction of a point of the best clean accuracy while clearly leading under corruption.
en.note: Higher is better for all columns. C10-C / C100-C are the corrupted benchmarks (19 corruption types x 5 severities). Numbers from Tables 1 and 2 of the paper.

en.text: The transfer-learning experiments broaden the picture across NLL, ECE, accuracy, and epistemic uncertainty, under both natural distribution shift (CINIC-10) and corruption shift. FoRDE improves on the baselines across the board, and its higher epistemic uncertainty on out-of-distribution data is a direct readout of the extra functional diversity that the method is explicitly designed to produce.

en.caption: Figure 4. Transfer-learning results. Across NLL, ECE, and accuracy on in-distribution, naturally shifted (CINIC-10), and corrupted test sets, FoRDE matches or beats the baselines; the rightmost panels show it also carries the highest epistemic uncertainty on out-of-distribution data, the signature of greater functional diversity.

zh.text: 损坏输入下的鲁棒性

主实验在 CIFAR-10、CIFAR-100 和 TinyImageNet 上进行，骨干网络为 ResNet-18 与 PreActResNet-18，集成含 10 个成员。鲁棒性在损坏基准 CIFAR-10-C、CIFAR-100-C 和 TinyImageNet-C 上测量，这些基准施加 19 种损坏类型、每种 5 个严重等级，并在干净指标之外报告损坏准确率（cA）、损坏 NLL 和损坏 ECE。结论一致：采用 PCA 长度尺度的 FoRDE 在每一项损坏指标上都是最强的，同时在干净数据上保持有竞争力。相比第二名，它在 CIFAR-10-C 上准确率提升约 +2.4%，在 CIFAR-100-C 上提升约 +1.3%。

zh.caption: 表1 ResNet-18、10 成员集成在 CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 上的干净准确率与损坏准确率（cA），5 个随机种子平均。FoRDE-PCA 干净准确率与最优仅差零点几个百分点，损坏下则明显领先。
zh.note: 所有列均为越高越好。C10-C / C100-C 为损坏基准（19 种损坏类型 × 5 个严重等级）。数字取自论文表 1 与表 2。

zh.text: 迁移学习实验把画面进一步铺开，覆盖 NLL、ECE、准确率和认知不确定性（epistemic uncertainty），并同时考察自然分布偏移（CINIC-10）和损坏偏移。FoRDE 在各项上都优于基线，而它在分布外数据上更高的认知不确定性，正是这套方法所要制造的额外功能多样性的直接读数。

zh.caption: 图4 迁移学习结果。在同分布、自然偏移（CINIC-10）与损坏测试集上，FoRDE 在 NLL、ECE 和准确率上都追平或超过基线；最右两列显示它在分布外数据上还拥有最高的认知不确定性，这正是更强功能多样性的标志。

en.title: From weights to input gradients: a cheaper place to make ensembles disagree
en.subtitle: FoRDE (ICLR 2024) repels ensemble members in input-gradient space, and the payoff shows up under image corruptions.

zh.title: 让集成模型「学会不一样」，换个空间成本更低
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · FoRDE：在输入梯度空间中互斥集成成员，换来图像损坏下更强的鲁棒性与校准。

en.text: A deep ensemble is a blunt instrument that works surprisingly well: train the same network a handful of times from different random seeds, average their predictions, and you usually get better accuracy, better calibration, and more graceful behavior on inputs the model has never seen. The reason is diversity. Each member settles into a different explanation of the data, and their disagreement is exactly what makes the average trustworthy.

So a natural idea is to stop leaving that diversity to chance and start enforcing it. Particle-based variational inference does this by treating each network as a particle and adding a repulsion term that actively pushes members apart during training. The catch is a question that turns out to matter a great deal: in what space should the members be pushed apart? Repel them in weight space and you fight against the fact that neural networks are wildly over-parameterized, so countless different weight vectors encode the same function. Repel them in function space and you run into an intractable comparison between whole functions, which forces shortcuts that tend to make the models underfit. In practice, neither approach had improved much on a plain deep ensemble.

This paper, First-order Repulsive Deep Ensembles (FoRDE), proposes a third space to disagree in. Instead of comparing weights or outputs, it pushes members apart in the space of their input gradients, the derivatives of the output with respect to the input. The choice is not cosmetic: input gradients characterize a function up to a translation, they are the same small size as the input rather than the enormous weight vector, and forcing them to differ forces each network to lean on different input features. The result is an ensemble that is markedly more robust and better calibrated when the input is corrupted.

en.text: The transfer-learning experiments broaden the picture across NLL, ECE, accuracy, and epistemic uncertainty, under both natural distribution shift (CINIC-10) and corruption shift. FoRDE improves on the baselines across the board, and its higher epistemic uncertainty on out-of-distribution data is a direct readout of the extra functional diversity that the method is explicitly designed to produce.

en.caption: Figure 4. Transfer-learning results. Across NLL, ECE, and accuracy on in-distribution, naturally shifted (CINIC-10), and corrupted test sets, FoRDE matches or beats the baselines; the rightmost panels show it also carries the highest epistemic uncertainty on out-of-distribution data, the signature of greater functional diversity.

zh.text: 深度集成（Deep Ensemble）是一种「简单却出奇有效」的做法：用不同随机种子把同一个网络训练好几遍，再把它们的预测取平均，往往就能同时拿到更高的准确率、更好的校准（calibration），以及在没见过的输入上更稳的表现。它之所以有效，关键在于多样性（diversity）：每个成员都落到了对数据的一种不同解释上，而它们之间的分歧，正是「取平均」值得信任的原因。

于是一个自然的想法是：不要把多样性交给运气，而是主动去制造它。基于粒子的变分推断（particle-based variational inference）就是这么做的：把每个网络当作一个粒子，在训练中加入一项互斥力（repulsion），主动把成员往两边推开。但这里藏着一个影响很大的问题：应该在哪个空间里把成员推开？在权重空间（weight space）里推，会和「神经网络严重过参数化」这个事实作对，因为无数个不同的权重其实编码的是同一个函数；在函数空间（function space）里推，又要面对「比较两个完整函数」这种难以计算的操作，逼着方法走近似捷径，反而容易欠拟合。结果是：这两条路都没能比普通深度集成好多少。

本文提出的 FoRDE（First-order Repulsive Deep Ensembles，一阶互斥深度集成）给出了第三个「制造分歧」的空间。它不比较权重，也不比较输出，而是在输入梯度（input gradient，即输出对输入的导数）空间里把成员推开。这个选择并不只是换个说法：输入梯度可以在「相差一个平移」的意义上唯一刻画一个函数；它的维度和输入一样小，远小于庞大的权重向量；而且强迫成员的输入梯度不同，等于强迫每个网络去依赖不同的输入特征。最终得到的集成，在输入被损坏（corruption）时明显更鲁棒、校准也更好。

zh.caption: 图1 一维回归玩具问题中，三个网络的输入梯度互斥过程。左：训练早期，三个模型都拟合了数据，却几乎处处一致，功能多样性很低。中：互斥项在每个数据点上，把成员的输入梯度（箭头）沿单位圆推开。右：训练结束时，三条函数真正分开，获得了让集成有价值的多样性。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02775 · 代码：https://github.com/AaltoPML/FoRDE
为什么「在哪个空间互斥」如此关键

要理解为什么输入梯度是个好地方，可以把神经网络的三种「视角」摆在一起比。权重是我们真正在优化的东西，但它并不适合用来衡量多样性：过参数化意味着两个差别很大的权重向量可能算出完全相同的函数，所以在权重空间里互相推开，可能白费力气，行为却没变。函数值是我们最终真正关心的，但比较完整的函数需要一个定义在函数空间上的核，计算代价很高；早期的互斥方法只能在训练输入上近似它，结果把模型推向欠拟合，相比普通集成几乎没有真实收益。

输入梯度恰好落在这两个极端之间。一个函数在「相差一个常数」的意义上由它的梯度场决定，所以两个网络只要输入梯度不同，就一定是不同的函数，而不是同一个函数的冗余改写。同时，梯度的维度和输入一样，对图像来说远小于权重向量，用核比较起来很便宜。还有一个后来被证明是实证关键的额外好处：输入梯度告诉你一个网络对哪些输入特征敏感。让两个成员的梯度指向不同方向，就等于让它们关注互补的特征，而这恰恰是输入之后被扰动时你最希望模型具备的性质。

en.subtitle: FoRDE (ICLR 2024) repels ensemble members in input-gradient space, and the payoff shows up under image corruptions.

zh.title: 让集成模型「学会不一样」，换个空间成本更低
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · FoRDE：在输入梯度空间中互斥集成成员，换来图像损坏下更强的鲁棒性与校准。

en.caption: Figure 1. Input-gradient repulsion in a 1D regression toy problem with three networks. Left: early in training the three models fit the data but agree almost everywhere, so functional diversity is low. Middle: the repulsion term pushes the members' input gradients (the arrows) apart on a unit circle at each data point. Right: by the end of training the three functions have genuinely diverged, gaining the diversity that makes an ensemble useful.

en.text: Why the space of repulsion matters

To see why input gradients are a good place to enforce disagreement, it helps to compare the three views of a neural network. Its weights are what you optimize, but they are a poor handle on diversity: over-parameterization means two very different weight vectors can compute the exact same function, so pushing weights apart can waste effort without changing behavior at all. Its function values are what you ultimately care about, but comparing entire functions requires a kernel over function space that is expensive to evaluate; earlier repulsive methods approximated it on training inputs only, which nudged the models toward underfitting and left little real gain over a vanilla ensemble.

Input gradients sit between these two extremes. A function is determined, up to an additive constant, by its gradient field, so two networks with different input gradients are guaranteed to be different functions, not redundant re-parameterizations. And a gradient has the dimensionality of the input, which for an image is far smaller than the weight vector, so it is cheap to compare with a kernel. There is a bonus that turns out to be the crux of the empirical story: the input gradient tells you which input features a network is sensitive to. Make two members' gradients point in different directions and you have made them attend to complementary features, which is precisely the property you want when the input is later perturbed.

en.title: From weights to input gradients: a cheaper place to make ensembles disagree
en.subtitle: FoRDE (ICLR 2024) repels ensemble members in input-gradient space, and the payoff shows up under image corruptions.

zh.title: 让集成模型「学会不一样」，换个空间成本更低
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · FoRDE：在输入梯度空间中互斥集成成员，换来图像损坏下更强的鲁棒性与校准。

en.text: A deep ensemble is a blunt instrument that works surprisingly well: train the same network a handful of times from different random seeds, average their predictions, and you usually get better accuracy, better calibration, and more graceful behavior on inputs the model has never seen. The reason is diversity. Each member settles into a different explanation of the data, and their disagreement is exactly what makes the average trustworthy.

So a natural idea is to stop leaving that diversity to chance and start enforcing it. Particle-based variational inference does this by treating each network as a particle and adding a repulsion term that actively pushes members apart during training. The catch is a question that turns out to matter a great deal: in what space should the members be pushed apart? Repel them in weight space and you fight against the fact that neural networks are wildly over-parameterized, so countless different weight vectors encode the same function. Repel them in function space and you run into an intractable comparison between whole functions, which forces shortcuts that tend to make the models underfit. In practice, neither approach had improved much on a plain deep ensemble.

This paper, First-order Repulsive Deep Ensembles (FoRDE), proposes a third space to disagree in. Instead of comparing weights or outputs, it pushes members apart in the space of their input gradients, the derivatives of the output with respect to the input. The choice is not cosmetic: input gradients characterize a function up to a translation, they are the same small size as the input rather than the enormous weight vector, and forcing them to differ forces each network to lean on different input features. The result is an ensemble that is markedly more robust and better calibrated when the input is corrupted.

en.caption: Figure 1. Input-gradient repulsion in a 1D regression toy problem with three networks. Left: early in training the three models fit the data but agree almost everywhere, so functional diversity is low. Middle: the repulsion term pushes the members' input gradients (the arrows) apart on a unit circle at each data point. Right: by the end of training the three functions have genuinely diverged, gaining the diversity that makes an ensemble useful.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02775 · Code: https://github.com/AaltoPML/FoRDE

zh.text: 多样性是真的吗：两个玩具实验
在大规模数字之前，两个玩具问题先把机制变得可见。在一维回归里，检验集成是否诚实的方式，是看它在远离训练数据的地方怎么表现：一个多样的集成应当在没见过的区域散开、报告高不确定性。FoRDE 明显比深度集成、以及权重空间和函数空间的互斥变体散得更开。

zh.caption: 图2 一维回归中的预测不确定性。在远离数据簇的区域，FoRDE（最右）散成明显更宽的置信带，超过深度集成、Weight-RDE 和 Function-RDE，说明它在最需要的地方拥有更强的功能多样性。

zh.text: 二维分类任务在平面上讲了同一个故事。用预测后验的熵来衡量，FoRDE 是唯一一个在训练簇之外几乎所有区域都保持不确定的方法，而不会在它本没有理由自信的地方，把一条清晰的决策边界自信地外推出去。

zh.caption: 图3 二维分类问题的预测熵图。暖色代表自信、冷色代表不确定。FoRDE（最右）在标注簇之外的整个输入平面上都保持高不确定性，而各基线在远离数据处仍然自信地下结论。

Takeaway

The lasting lesson is that the space in which you enforce diversity matters as much as how hard you enforce it. Weight space is wasteful because of over-parameterization; function space is intractable to compare directly. Input gradients sit in between: small enough to compare cheaply, expressive enough to make members genuinely different functions, and meaningful enough that pushing them apart makes members rely on complementary features. Paired with data-driven PCA lengthscales, that choice buys more robust, better-calibrated ensembles under real-world input corruptions, at about three times the training cost.

在大规模数字之前，两个玩具问题先把机制变得可见。在一维回归里，检验集成是否诚实的方式，是看它在远离训练数据的地方怎么表现：一个多样的集成应当在没见过的区域散开、报告高不确定性。FoRDE 明显比深度集成、以及权重空间和函数空间的互斥变体散得更开。

zh.text: 损坏输入下的鲁棒性

主实验在 CIFAR-10、CIFAR-100 和 TinyImageNet 上进行，骨干网络为 ResNet-18 与 PreActResNet-18，集成含 10 个成员。鲁棒性在损坏基准 CIFAR-10-C、CIFAR-100-C 和 TinyImageNet-C 上测量，这些基准施加 19 种损坏类型、每种 5 个严重等级，并在干净指标之外报告损坏准确率（cA）、损坏 NLL 和损坏 ECE。结论一致：采用 PCA 长度尺度的 FoRDE 在每一项损坏指标上都是最强的，同时在干净数据上保持有竞争力。相比第二名，它在 CIFAR-10-C 上准确率提升约 +2.4%，在 CIFAR-100-C 上提升约 +1.3%。

zh.caption: 表1 ResNet-18、10 成员集成在 CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 上的干净准确率与损坏准确率（cA），5 个随机种子平均。FoRDE-PCA 干净准确率与最优仅差零点几个百分点，损坏下则明显领先。

zh.text: 迁移学习实验把画面进一步铺开，覆盖 NLL、ECE、准确率和认知不确定性（epistemic uncertainty），并同时考察自然分布偏移（CINIC-10）和损坏偏移。FoRDE 在各项上都优于基线，而它在分布外数据上更高的认知不确定性，正是这套方法所要制造的额外功能多样性的直接读数。

zh.caption: 图4 迁移学习结果。在同分布、自然偏移（CINIC-10）与损坏测试集上，FoRDE 在 NLL、ECE 和准确率上都追平或超过基线；最右两列显示它在分布外数据上还拥有最高的认知不确定性，这正是更强功能多样性的标志。
